label: early input q (or e/g after certain letters) at original positions 2-3
explanation: Fires only in the original input phase, almost entirely at steps 2 and 3 (99% of mass; a trace at step 4; never at t<2, at the delimiter or in the copy phase). It is token-selective: input q gives 69% of the mass and nearly all of the strongest activations (q at t=2-3 is active 88% of the time and covers 92% of the top activation quartile). The top examples are q right after d (e.g. h k d q). Weaker firing comes from e and g, and less from l and v. Whether these fire depends on the earlier prefix: d, r, h, j, k, y or 0 among the preceding tokens helps. That dependence is only roughly captured, which is why precision is incomplete. It almost never fires on repeat occurrences of a token (in_first=1 holds 96% of mass). It does not fire on other tokens or at later positions.
